questions.q: What first step does the book suggest for identifying your best self?
a: Write down your positive traits on a piece of paper
List your biggest fears on paper
Memorize inspirational quotes daily
Create a vision board of future goals
questions.why: The summary says to write all positive traits on paper to recognize your best self.

questions.q: Why does the summary say most people didn't learn to reach their full potential early?
a: Schools offered no curriculum on finding and connecting with your full potential
Parents discouraged any ambition from a young age
Media promoted instant success over effort
Society valued conformity over individuality
questions.why: It notes there was no curriculum in school for discovering and using full potential.

questions.q: What three-part statement does the book recommend completing to confront a fear?
a: My fear is…; It’s keeping me from…; My plan to stop it becoming reality is…
I feel…; I will…; I succeed…
Fear is bad; I avoid it; I ignore it
I think…; I doubt…; I hope…
questions.why: The summary lists those three statements to write on paper for each fear.

questions.q: How does the book advise you to uncover the underlying theme of your fears?
a: Journal answers to “What fears do I have…?” and examine them closely
Talk to a therapist about your worries
Take a personality test to identify fears
Meditate without focusing on any issue
questions.why: It suggests journaling the question about fears and digging deep to find a theme.

questions.q: Which self‑care practice is highlighted as a simple way to reduce stress?
a: Mindful breathing
Watching TV to distract yourself
Skipping meals to save time
Ignoring emotions until they pass
questions.why: The summary mentions mindful breathing as a quick method to calm and gain perspective.
